title: Uniqueness of the optimal double-barrier strategy for impulse control with a level-dependent intensity of bankruptcy (Theorem 6.1)
author: Dante Mata
work: Impulse control in a spectrally negative Levy model with a level-dependent intensity of bankruptcy
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the article's main theorem (source label thm.unique, printed as Theorem 6.1): under a log-convex tail of the Levy measure there is a unique optimal double-barrier impulse control strategy for the Omega-model dividend problem, and the lower barrier is zero exactly when the transaction cost dominates the threshold beta_max. The unit is not a qualification exercise because the counted claim cannot be reached without the whole source-local analysis that the unit retains and that the proof body carries: the Omega-model with a state-dependent bankruptcy intensity and its omega-killed spectrally negative Levy process, the generalised (Omega) scale functions defined through an integral equation with their analytical properties under a log-convex tail, the performance function of a double-barrier strategy and the admissible impulse strategies with their Meyer-Ito decomposition, the verification lemma with its complete martingale proof and the localisation argument, the optimality theorem, and then the uniqueness proof itself, which reduces the two-dimensional minimisation of g into the auxiliary functions g_1 and g_0, proves that C* is a singleton by a mean-value-theorem contradiction on the strictly monotone generalised scale function, proves that g_0 has a unique minimiser by a two-sided asymptotic argument, and finally separates the three regimes a*>0 with beta<beta_max, a*>0 with beta>=beta_max and a*=0 by comparing g_1 with the generalised scale function. Impulse control, Omega-model ruin and fluctuation theory of spectrally negative Levy processes combined into a complete uniqueness proof is research-level stochastic control, well beyond ordinary PhD qualifying examinations.
